title: Collateral and Title Guideline: The Release Price of a Homesite on a Farmstead Split — Farm Real Estate Loans
content:
For a farmstead split on a Farm Real Estate Loans mortgage, the release price is the release premium percentage of the homesite's share of principal, rounded to cents, the share being the principal balance times the homesite's value divided by the value still mortgaged, and rounded to cents.

## Inputs

| Input | Source on the loan's records |
|---|---|
| Release premium percentage | the product's release premium |
| Homesite's value | the appraised value at mortgage of the parcel of land use farmstead still mortgaged |
| Value still mortgaged | every parcel mortgaged to the loan less every parcel released from it, at appraised value |
| Principal balance | the principal balance on the release date |

## Order of rounding

1. The homesite's share of principal is the principal balance multiplied by the homesite's value and divided by the value still mortgaged, rounded to cents.
2. The release price is the release premium percentage of that rounded share, rounded to cents.

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

A loan with a principal balance of USD 500000.00 on the release date has parcels still mortgaged appraised at USD 1250000, among them the homesite at USD 150000. Take a release premium of 110 percent.

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Share: 500000.00 multiplied by 150000, divided by 1250000 | 60000.00 |
| Release price: 110 percent of 60000.00 | **66000.00** |

At a release premium of 125 percent the same share would give a release price of 75000.00.

A parcel already released from the loan counts in neither the homesite's value nor the value still mortgaged.
